headline: Board of Water Supply

meeting.summary: The Board of Water Supply put off two items and heard the full desalination study cannot be released for security reasons.
meeting.recap: The board approved its September 17, 2026 minutes with five ayes.[[0:01:36]] A testifier asked the board to take up a Hawaiian Homelands wells agreement with the water department in November.[[0:03:41]] The testifier asked for a legal opinion on whether the agreement breaks the Upcountry community plan.[[0:04:05]] The board put off a talk with the water and planning directors about subdivision water until next meeting.[[0:11:51]] The water director said only a summary of the desalination (seawater-to-fresh-water) study is online.[[0:34:27]] The director said Homeland Security would not allow release of the full study for security reasons.[[0:34:31]] A testifier asked why the budget has money for a new desalination study when the first can't be seen.[[0:37:29]] The director said a releasable West Maui water plan should be out by the end of the year.[[0:40:30]] The director said the new money would fund a next phase looking closer at specific sites.[[0:41:34]] The next meeting is November 19th at 1:30.[[0:44:00]]
decided: discussion with the water supply and planning directors on securing water supply for subdivision applications: The board agreed to put the item off to its next meeting.
meeting.next: The chair said the planning director will be asked to come back at the next meeting. A member asked that the planning item be placed at the top of the next agenda, and the chair said she would discuss it. A member said he will draft questions for the board's lawyer about the duties of ex officio (non-voting, by-position) members. The board's lawyer said a future agenda item could discuss sending a letter to the mayor, if the board approves it. The director said the department is working with the Senate to let Hawaiʻi use federal desalination funds.
